title: The Unwritten Clock
premise: In the winter of 1919, in a river town straddling a border about to be redrawn, Ivo Dunmore completes the master mapmaker's final atlas — one that contains survey marks proving the armistice commission's boundary will cut the town's water supply in half. When the bridge closes for the season, Ivo, the master's widow Lena, and a checkpoint sergeant who once loved her become entangled in a race to carry the evidence south before the treaty ink dries. Ivo must choose between the loyalty he owes the dead man and the truth the living deserve, and in the end he burns the atlas itself, teaching the town's children to draw the maps from memory — an act of defiance no checkpoint can search.
about_author: Hazel Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border survey records from post-war Europe. She writes from a converted signal box on the coast, where she still keeps her grandfather's brass compass.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the dead master's cold workshop, Ivo finishes inking the final plates of the atlas while Lena quietly catalogues her husband's papers. He finds a sealed envelope of survey coordinates he doesn't understand. The beat is quiet dread: the world feels orderly on paper, and Ivo clings to that order.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo walks the riverbank to verify the last survey mark and realizes the coordinates describe a border that would sever the town's waterworks. He tells no one. The emotional beat is the first crack in his loyalty — knowledge as a burden he isn't sure he wants to carry.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dusk
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Soldiers post the notice: the bridge closes for the season at week's end; all maps and documents are subject to inspection at three new checkpoints. Lena burns her husband's letters but keeps the atlas. Her beat is grief sharpening into resolve — she has buried one man for his work and won't bury his life's meaning.

chapters.title: The Sergeant's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sergeant Brann's POV. At the first checkpoint, Brann processes travelers and recognizes Lena's name on the manifest. Flashbacks reveal his history with her and the master. His beat is divided loyalty: he owes the uniform his honesty and the widow his silence, and he hasn't decided which.

chapters.title: A Cartography of Small Things
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo copies the damning coordinates into miniature — hidden in the compass rose of a pocket map, in the stitching of a satchel, in the margins of a school primer. Lena helps him. The beat is intimacy: two people learning each other through careful, conspiratorial work, love arriving sideways.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo attempts to cross with the primer hidden in a schoolchild's bundle and is stopped by Brann, who recognizes the master's hand in the marginalia — and lets him pass, asking nothing. The beat is vertigo: mercy from the man he feared most, and the terrifying knowledge that Brann now knows.

chapters.title: What Lena Kept
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena reveals she has known about the coordinates for weeks and has been feeding the commission false copies to buy time. Ivo feels betrayed, then understands: she was protecting him. The beat is rupture and repair — loyalty and truth colliding inside the house itself.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Brann's POV. Brann's superior arrives to audit the checkpoint and demands the seizure of all cartographic material, including the primer Ivo passed through. Brann falsifies the ledger to cover his earlier mercy. The beat is a man crossing his own line — no longer loyal to the uniform, not yet to the town.

chapters.title: The Armistice Hour
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the night the treaty is to be signed, Ivo, Lena, and Brann converge at the frozen bridge for a final crossing as the third checkpoint seals. Brann holds the gate open for exactly as long as he dares. The beat is the climax: three people, one truth, and a river of ice between them and the future.

chapters.title: Maps Drawn from Memory
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing with a communal voice. The crossing succeeds, but the commission's decision arrives too late to matter on paper — so Ivo burns the atlas in the workshop hearth and begins teaching the town's children to draw their own maps from memory. The beat is resolution: identity isn't what borders say you are, but what you carry and pass on.
